questions.q: In the lab scenario, why can't the raw scan output alone tell you which of the two servers to fix first?
options: Because the scanner always lists findings in the correct priority order already
Because CVE identifiers are randomly generated and carry no technical meaning
Because the scan only found a finding on one of the two servers
Because the scanner's output lists the same CVE and the same severity score for both servers, with no business context attached
questions.explain: Two identical-looking scan lines give you no principled reason to prioritize one over the other without CMDB correlation.

questions.q: What specifically separates the two findings once Vulnerability Response correlates them against the CMDB?
options: One CI is tagged as supporting the QA test environment; the other is tagged, through CSDM relationships, as supporting the Patient Scheduling Business Service that clinicians depend on
The CVE identifier changes once correlation runs
Correlation reveals that neither server actually has the vulnerability
Correlation only changes the severity score, not the business context
questions.explain: The CSDM relationship from CI up to Business Service is exactly what tells two identical-severity findings apart.

questions.q: What is the correct prioritization decision in this scenario, and why?
options: Both findings should be ignored since they share the same CVE
Fix the Patient Scheduling production database server first, because CMDB/CSDM correlation shows it supports a critical Business Service, despite identical CVE and severity
Fix whichever server has the alphabetically earlier hostname
Fix the QA test server first because it was discovered first in the scan output
questions.explain: Business risk, surfaced through CMDB and CSDM correlation, should drive remediation order — not raw severity alone.

questions.q: What specific evidence turns this scenario from a Vulnerability Response problem into a Security Incident Response problem?
options: The vulnerability scan simply flagged the CVE as Critical severity
The CMDB record for the server was found to be out of date
The QA test server's finding was closed out as remediated
Log evidence suggesting the vulnerability on the Patient Scheduling server wasn't just present but had already been actively exploited
questions.explain: A confirmed or strongly suspected exploitation event is exactly the trigger for opening a Security Incident, per Lesson 15's distinction.

questions.q: In the sketched Security Incident record, why does the response move to Containment immediately, before Eradication or Recovery?
options: Containment should actually happen last, after the server is already reconnected
Because Recovery must always happen before any investigation begins
Containment and Eradication are the same step and happen simultaneously by default
To stop the active threat from spreading further — isolating the server, rotating credentials, blocking suspicious traffic — before the root cause is even fully understood or removed
questions.explain: Containment comes first on purpose, exactly as Lesson 15 established — stop the damage now, understand and remove the root cause next.
